subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for September 22, 2026.
Today we will review 2 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

sentences: Story 2 is about Alveolar Ventilation Efficiency Assessed via Capnography is Associated with Improved Outcomes in Pediatric Cardiac Arrest..
This is a recent research article from American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in children (≤18 years) with invasive airways and capnography data, how should we interpret Exposure or intervention stated in the title/objective. compared with Comparator or control group stated in the methods/results, if present.?
Among 99 events (median age: 0.34 [0.04, 3.26] yrs), median AOI was 0.38 [0.25, 0.53].

Event-level average AOI ≥0.35 was associated with improved survival to hospital discharge (aRR 1.53 [CI95 1.03, 2.28], p = 0.04) and favorable neurological outcome (aRR 1.56 [CI95 1.01, 2.41], p = 0.04) compared to AOI <0.35.
Findings were robust when excluding E-CPR patients.
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.
The bedside implication is this: Use as an awareness item; read the full article before applying it clinically.
Useful English phrase: these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the details of design and applicability matter.

script.heading: Outro
sentences: That wraps up today's journal club style update.
Before applying any finding, check the full source, the absolute effect size, and your local ICU context.
For English practice, repeat one academic phrase from each article out loud.

articles.summary: From June 2024-May 2026, 481 patients were enrolled, aged 65.4 (16.8) [mean (standard deviation)] years. The most common diagnoses were neurologic or neurosurgical (175, 36.4%), cardiovascular or vascular (97, 20.2%) and trauma (59, 12.3%). Of 2305 elicited end-of-life wishes, 2280 (98.9%) were implemented. Personnel eliciting wishes included nurses (169, 35.1%), social workers (152, 31.6%) and the project coordinator (99, 20.6%). Common wishes were tributes and keepsakes (820, 35.6%), acts to humanize the patient (374, 16.2%) and facilitating connections (248, 10.8%).

articles.title: Alveolar Ventilation Efficiency Assessed via Capnography is Associated with Improved Outcomes in Pediatric Cardiac Arrest.
articles.source: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.summary: Airway opening index (AOI) is a metric recently described in adults to infer airway patency during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). The underlying premise is that higher AOI values suggest more patent airways, which leads to improved ventilation/ outcomes. 1) To quantitatively describe AOI during pediatric CPR and 2) to evaluate the association of AOI with outcomes. Prospective multicenter observational cohort study of children (≤18 years) with invasive airways and capnography data. AOI was calculated as the average of ((delta CO2)/max CO2) associated with each chest compression during a ventilation (range: 0 [closed] to 1 [open]).
